steps.headline: Which reviewers should stay fixed?
steps.today: The live rules run a fresh-eyes tester twice, a code reviewer, a contract writer and a grader on every full feature. My rewrite on this branch made all of them optional checks you choose.
steps.problem: Making everything optional risks losing the code reviewer, the one with a strong record. Keeping everything fixed keeps the noise and the contracts you dislike.
steps.proposal: Pick how fixed the reviewers are.
steps.checked: Read the four reviewer briefs, 72 review files, and your past remarks about them, today.

options.label: Keep every reviewer on every full feature
pros: Nothing already decided is lost.
cons: Keeps the contract and grader, which never changed an outcome you noticed.
About 13 helper runs per feature.

options.label: Code reviewer always runs on risky work; the tester and grader are checks I suggest and you choose; no contract
pros: Keeps the reviewer with the strongest record, where it paid off: security, your data, background work, anything cross-device.
Matches what you already do when moving fast.
cons: A build that looks harmless but is risky could miss its code review if I judge the risk wrongly.

options.label: Every reviewer is a check I suggest and you choose
pros: Fewest fixed steps.
You see and edit the whole list each time.
cons: A suggested code review can be declined on work that needed it.
